1 · The one fix that is not optional: the campaign is over

The deck still presents a running experiment. By 3 September that will be three weeks stale and anyone who has spoken to the collaboration will know it. More importantly, it undersells you: “still taking data” is a weaker statement than “the dataset is complete, and here it is.” Three places say it:

WhereWhat it says nowWhat it should say
D0 “Where things stand”“taking production statistics as of today” + the flag “running as this talk is given — numbers are 2026-08-09”The campaign ran 28 June – 10 August and is complete; four chambers live to the end; analysis ongoing. Retire the flag or restamp it “dataset final 2026-08-10”.
D6 stat tile“~1.7 TB production statistics banked since 2026-08-02, still running”The final production number. (Keep 1.65 TB if you want the “since 8-02” framing, but say the campaign closed at 17.9 TB total / 41.8 M events. The 1.7 TB was a mid-campaign snapshot of the production phase only.)
Summary, bullet 3“taking production statistics”“ran the full 2026 campaign — 41.8 M events, 17.9 TB, dataset complete”. Proposed slide P8 is a drop-in replacement.

Proposed slide P1 (“Six weeks of beam: the dataset is complete”) turns this from a fix into a feature — see §3. Even if you adopt nothing else, make these three edits.

2 · Clarity for a first-contact audience

The deck is honest and figure-rich, and the narrative spine (problem → detector → environment → what we did → what we get) is genuinely good. The gaps are all of one kind: things the deck knows so well it forgot to say.

2.1 DREAM is never introduced — and it carries the whole Status section

The first time the audience meets the word is the title of D1, “What the γ flash does to a DREAM channel.” Nothing before it says the chambers are read out by charge-integrating front-end electronics called DREAM, or that a chamber is 1,024 channels of it. The entire Status argument — “the chamber is fine, the front end is not” — rests on a distinction the audience has not been given. One sentence fixes it; the natural host is the setup slide that introduces the chambers (“+ four Micromegas micro-TPCs”), or D1’s own caption:

suggested line “Each chamber’s 1,024 strips are read out by DREAM front-end ASICs — charge-integrating amplifiers, 50–600 fC full scale — the same chain as the cosmic bench.”

2.2 M3 appears one slide before it is explained

Slide “A cosmic muon, reconstructed” (main flow 12) says “the independent M3 reference-telescope track threading it” — but the bench, and with it the idea of a reference telescope, arrives on the next slide. If the bench slide survives the Alexandra decision, consider swapping the two; if it gets cut to a one-liner, the event-display caption needs its own clause: “M3 — the four-plane Micromegas reference telescope that brackets the chamber on the bench.” The efficiency and resolution slides lean on the same unexplained recipe (“χ² < 1.0 & NClus = 4” appears on the efficiency caption with no gloss — it can simply be cut from the spoken layer; it is caption armour, not talk material).

2.3 Bench chambers are det-numbers; n_TOF chambers are arm letters — and the two are never joined

The characterization slides certify det3 at 93.5 %; the Status slides run chambers A–D. A first-contact listener has no way to know whether the chamber you characterized is even in the experiment. One line somewhere (D0, or the fleet backup slide) closing the loop — “the four beam chambers A–D are <which dets> of the bench fleet” — would do it. I did not find the mapping stated anywhere in the deck and did not want to guess it; you know it off-hand.

2.4 Why the physics lives at milliseconds is assumed, never said

D4 shades “where the thermal neutrons arrive” and D7 shows the overlap, but no slide says why the signal is thermal and late: capture cross-sections grow as 1/v, and slow neutrons take milliseconds to fly 20 m — so time-of-flight puts the richest capture window exactly on top of the recovery window. That single causal sentence is what makes the whole Status section land for an outsider. Proposed slide P3 (the trigger) opens with it; if P3 is not adopted, put the sentence on D4.

3 · The eight proposed slides (pages 72–80)

All at the end of the deck behind the “Proposed · 13 Aug” divider. Each slide’s HTML comment in index.html carries slot, provenance and adoption notes; this is the argument.

SlideWhy / where
P1Six weeks of beam: the dataset is completeThe campaign-statistics slide you asked for, and the fix for §1. Daily events figure with the 41.8 M cumulative curve and the two phase boundaries; tiles 41.8 M / 17.9 TB / 436,373 pulses / 78.6 %. The order-of-magnitude rate climb between 14 and 26 July is the narrative hook: it is the trigger and operating-point work visibly paying off. Slot: right after D0, or absorb D0. Figure: ntof_run_report (counts = decoded_root nt entries, independent of matching).
P2Beam availability, day by dayBackup behind P1 for the inevitable “how much was the machine?” Total downtime only — the report explicitly distrusts the PS-vs-n_TOF blame split, so the slide never quotes it.
P3The trigger lives in the thermal window — by designThe thermal-trigger slide you asked for, and it fixes §2.4. Left: recorded trigger rate vs neutron arrival time against Geant4 (the 5.3 ms peak reproduces; normalisation 2.1× high, per-wall 1.1–2.6×, under investigation). Right: why milliseconds, the wall∧plastic 20 ns coincidence at ½ / 0.90 MIP, the three-way cross-check (emulation vs hardware trigger edges to 12–17 %), and the honest punchline — simulation says 96 % of trigger legs are Al-capture γs. Slot: Status · Operating in it, next to D6. The existing backup B3 (threshold table) stays as its depth.
P4The flash, weighed: ~10² nC — and dead time follows the chargeThe single γ-flash-charge slide you asked for: D2’s “how much” and D5’s “so what” on one page (both figures already in the deck), so the 15-minute cut spends one slide, not two, and the audience sees the measurement and the power law together. D2/D3/D5 stay in backup untouched.
P5Beam tracks image the ³He capsuleThe imaging headliner, upgraded from run_79 fans to the run_145 image: back-projection focal spot inside the r = 10 mm bore, and the spot-focusing scale is an in-situ drift-velocity measurement — 36.1 µm/ns, 15 % below clean-gas, same direction and size as the bench trace-water effect. That closes the biggest caveat D8 carried (transferred v). 51 % of predictable tracks externally confirmed by the SiPM segment and plastic bar they point at. PRELIMINARY stays on the face: one sub-run, arm A.
P6All four arms point back at the targetThe 2×2 four-arm coloured-track composite (run_145). One slide that says “this is not one lucky chamber”: bundles ordered at the wall on every arm, converging at the target plane, nulls quoted. Slot: after P5, or backup if the section is tight. If adopted, D8 → backup.
P7Next: from single tracks to pairsThe forward-looking close you asked for. A real two-track event in one chamber (ev1054, July scan) as the visual — captioned honestly as a hits-basis demonstration with a two-fold pairing ambiguity — beside the sober status: multi-track candidates shipped and bit-identical, the merged-cluster two-track forward fit the one unbuilt piece, 41.8 M banked events with an Al-pair-dominated trigger as the calibration sample, and σ(p)/p ≲ 30 % as the MPGD question to leave the room with. Absorbs D10’s “next” bullet; D10’s “what did not work” bullet is worth keeping wherever it lands.
P8Summary, updatedDrop-in replacement for the current Summary: campaign-final numbers, closes forward (pairs) instead of backward (the flash). If adopted, edit the existing Summary in place rather than keeping two.
What I deliberately did not make: a yield or reach slide. The no-yield decision (framing (c), 2026-08-10) is respected everywhere — P7 talks about the search machinery and the tracker requirement, never about expected events. The thermal-rates backup table stays where it is, ready for questions.

6 · Number discrepancies found while fact-checking

WhereFinding
vinsituThe committed run_145 note and the end-of-run report both say 36.1 µm/ns (k = 1.18); a 36.3 figure was floating in working notes. The slides use 36.1.
Trigger data/sim excessCommitted numbers: 2.1× overall, per-wall 1.1–2.6× (429 vs 205 legs/pulse). An older “2–5×, accidentals” recollection is superseded; P3 quotes the committed values and says “under investigation” rather than asserting accidentals.
17.9 TB / 83 runs / 162 runs / 2,705 sub-runsThese are hard-coded strings in ntof_run_report/make_report.py, unlike 41.8 M and 78.6 % which are computed at build time. Fine for the talk; worth knowing which numbers would silently survive a data change.
P1 figure titleThe events figure says “2 July – 10 August” (first DREAM events on disk) while the campaign is 28 June – 10 August (setup weeks). The P1 caption uses the campaign dates; if that reads as a clash, regenerate the figure title from figures_local.py.
1.7 TB vs 17.9 TBNot a contradiction: 1.65 TB was the production-phase subset as of 8-09; 17.9 TB is the full campaign on EOS. D6’s tile should say which it means (§1).
